research_question: Can a local model build a source-grounded business-semantic graph from schema and column documentation for a database with no declared foreign keys, and does graph-aware retrieval help recover tables used by held-out questions?
core_hypothesis: A Qwen-generated, evidence-linked business graph can recover useful physical relationships in a zero-declared-FK database and improve table retrieval over raw schema BM25 on this single exploratory database.
experiment_layer: exploratory feasibility pilot; not mainline paper evidence

methods: schema_bm25: table names, column names, column descriptions, and value descriptions
flat_graph_bm25: graph-generated node text flattened by mapped table
typed_graph: graph node scores plus fixed 0.25 one-hop relation contribution
evaluation.sql_parse_failure_policy: retain as parse-failure denominator; exclude from table-ranking metrics and report count

budget_and_stopping.success_signal: valid evidence-referenced graph, all reported physical bindings resolve to the frozen schema, at least one proposed physical join is observed in BIRD Gold SQL, and typed-graph Recall@3 or MRR exceeds schema_bm25
budget_and_stopping.stop_condition: stop after the single generation and one frozen CPU evaluation; do not prompt-tune or add model calls if the signal is absent
budget_and_stopping.interpretation_limit: one BIRD train database and Gold-SQL table/JOIN references are retrieval proxies, not human business-semantics labels or independent benchmark results
